question.prompt: Lines \(L_1,\) \(L_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(L_{100}\) are distinct. All lines \(L_{4n},\) \(n\) a positive integer, are parallel to each other. All lines \(L_{4n-3},\) \(n\) a positive integer, pass through a given point \(A.\) The maximum number of points of intersection of pairs of lines from the complete set \(\{L_1,L_2,\ldots,L_{100}\}\) is

solutions.explanation:
Two distinct lines have at most one intersection, so begin by counting unordered pairs of lines. We must then account for pairs that do not intersect and pairs that meet at the same point.

There are \(25\) specified parallel lines, with indices \(4,8,\ldots,100\), and \(25\) specified lines through \(A\), with indices \(1,5,\ldots,97\). These groups are disjoint. Among all
\[
\binom{100}{2}=4950
\]
line pairs, the
\[
\binom{25}{2}=300
\]
pairs within the parallel group contribute no intersections. The \(300\) pairs within the group through \(A\) all contribute the single point \(A\).

The remaining \(4950-300-300=4350\) pairs can contribute at most one point each. This proves the upper bound
\[
4350+1=4351.
\]
To show that this maximum is possible, start with \(25\) distinct horizontal lines, none through \(A\). Choose \(25\) distinct nonhorizontal lines through \(A\). These create no triple intersection away from \(A\): two lines through \(A\) meet only there, and two horizontal lines never meet.

Now add the remaining \(50\) lines one at a time. For each new line, choose a direction different from all existing directions and choose its position so that it avoids every existing intersection point. This is possible because there are only finitely many forbidden directions and points. Once a direction is chosen, each forbidden point rules out just one parallel translate of the new line.

Each added line therefore meets all earlier lines at distinct new points. In the completed arrangement, every pair outside the two special groups intersects, and no two such pairs share an intersection point. Together with \(A\), this gives exactly \(\boxed{4351}\) points, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Count line pairs and show the bound is attainable
